repo.description:
### Summary

The OAuth token endpoint treated PKCE as a substitute for client authentication, so a confidential client's authorization code could be exchanged for tokens without the registered client secret ever being presented.

### Details

Client authentication in `oauth-token.service.ts` was keyed off whether the authorization code carried a PKCE challenge rather than off the client's registered type. The authorization endpoint in `oauth-authorization.service.ts` required a `code_challenge` on every request, so every issued code was classified as a PKCE flow, and on that branch the client secret was verified only when the caller volunteered one - omitting it skipped verification entirely and the exchange continued. The branch that required a secret for confidential clients was therefore unreachable for the authorization-code grant, even though the refresh-token grant on the same service still enforced it. PKCE and client authentication protect different things: the verifier proves possession of the code, while the secret authenticates the registered client itself.

### Impact

Possession of an authorization code and its matching PKCE verifier was sufficient to mint an access token and a 60-day refresh token in the name of a confidential client, with no knowledge of that client's secret. An attacker who captured a code and verifier - through a leaked redirect, a malicious component in the client application, or a raced exchange - needed no second factor to complete the exchange, and the confidential-client registration provided no defence in depth for initial token issuance. No NocoDB session is required at the token endpoint.

### Credit

This issue was reported by [@mantraak](https://github.com/mantraak).
repo.summary: Client Authentication Bypass in OAuth Token Exchange
